{{Short description|44th season of the National Hurling League}} {{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox GAA League |league = 1974–75 National Hurling League |image = |dates = 29 September 1974 – 25 May 1975 |teams = |team1 = Galway |captain1 = |manager1 = |titles = 3rd |team2 = |captain2 = |manager2 = |two= Westmeath |previous = [[1973–74 National Hurling League|1973–74]] |next = [[1975–76 National Hurling League|1975–76]] }} The '''1974–75 National Hurling League''' was the 44th season of the [[National Hurling League]].{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/general/leagues/nhlrecords.aspx|title=National Hurling League Results 1925-2009|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=18 April 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100805063526/http://www.hoganstand.com/general/leagues/nhlrecords.aspx|archive-date=2010-08-05|url-status=dead}} ==Division 1== {{Infobox football league season |competition=[[National Hurling League|National Hurling League Division 1]] |season=1974-75 |winners=[[Galway GAA|Galway]]
3rd National League title
Captain: [[John Connolly (hurler)|John Connolly]] |relegated= |continentalcup1= |continentalcup1 qualifiers= |continentalcup2= |continentalcup2 qualifiers= |league topscorer=[[File: Colours of Tipperary.svg|border|20px]] [[Francis Loughnane]] (5-35) |best goalkeeper= |biggest home win= |biggest away win= |highest scoring= |matches= 47 |total goals= |longest wins= |longest unbeaten= |longest winless= |longest losses= |highest attendance= |lowest attendance= |attendance= |average attendance= |prevseason=[[1973-74 National Hurling League|1973-74]] |nextseason=[[1975-76 National Hurling League|1975-76]] |updated=20 March 2017 }} [[Cork GAA|Cork]] came into the season as defending champions of the [[1973-74 National Hurling League|1973-74 season]]. On 25 May 1975, [[Galway GAA|Galway]] won the title following a 4-9 to 4-6 win over [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in the final. It was their 3rd league title overall and their first since [[1950-51 National Hurling League|1950-51]].{{cite web|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/1975-the-summer-the-west-was-stirred-from-its-slumber-206477.html|title=1975: The summer the West was stirred from its slumber|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=5 September 2012|accessdate=8 May 2017|first=Enda|last=McEvoy}} [[Wicklow GAA|Wicklow]] were relegated to Division 2 after losing all of their group stage matches in Division 1B.
